title: US Law Firm Willkie Partners With OpenAI
author: Willkie Farr & Gallagher · Artificial Lawyer

st.t: Operating model: AI shifts bargaining across providers
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s core framing of AI as an operating-model transformation by describing firmwide deployment, proprietary technology development, secure workflow integration and service-delivery redesign. It is evidence of strategic intent rather than measured returns, and it does not substantively assess shifts toward legal departments or ALSPs, or changes in pricing and bargaining power.
qs: ‘The opportunity AI presents is not simply to work faster, but to rethink how legal services are delivered, how institutional knowledge is leveraged and how clients are served.

They added that the OpenAI ‘collaboration builds upon Willkie Works, the firm’s AI and innovation organization, which is focused on developing proprietary technologies and integrating them safely and securely into legal and business workflows’.

st.t: Workflow control: Foundation models challenge specialist interfaces
st.an: The report supports the cluster’s proposition by documenting OpenAI’s direct, firmwide role in Willkie’s legal and business workflows, including ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex and proprietary platform development. It also reinforces the cluster’s caution that this is commercial entry and co-development rather than proof of product maturity, improved outcomes or displacement: Artificial Lawyer describes OpenAI’s legal offering as still awaiting formal rollout.
qs: # US Law Firm Willkie Partners With OpenAI  *Willkie Farr & Gallagher, Artificial Lawyer — Willkie / Artificial Lawyer (2026)*  ## Full Text — "US Law Firm Willkie Partners With OpenAI," Artificial Lawyer, 22 July 2026  Major US law firm, Willkie, is partnering with OpenAI to develop ‘AI solutions across the firm’s legal and business operations, including a firmwide rollout of ChatGPT Enterprise’.
The move comes ahead of OpenAI formally rolling out its own legal vertical capabilities, which it hired ex-Ironclad founder Jason Boehmig to lead (see his comment below).

kp.k: OpenAI collaboration targets firmwide deployment and proprietary platform development
kp.d: Willkie's 22 July 2026 announcement describes a collaboration covering legal and business operations, including a firmwide rollout of ChatGPT Enterprise and access to OpenAI models, technical resources and enterprise capabilities. The firm presents this as accelerating its proprietary platforms through Willkie Works; the announcement describes intended benefits rather than quantified results.
qs: Willkie today announced a collaboration with OpenAI that will accelerate the development and deployment of next-generation artificial intelligence solutions across the firm's legal and business operations, including a firmwide rollout of ChatGPT Enterprise.

OpenAI frontier models will help power the next generation of these platforms, enabling Willkie to accelerate the design, testing and deployment of new AI-driven capabilities across legal and business functions.

kp.k: Existing platforms span legal workflows, business intelligence and training
kp.d: Willkie reports an existing proprietary portfolio embedded across legal, business and client-facing workflows. Its platforms cover a unified enterprise interface, financial and matter intelligence, attorney development, private funds secondaries, and claimant analysis and litigation. These are reported applications and purposes, not measured evidence of effectiveness or changes in staffing.
qs: Through Willkie Works, the firm has developed a growing portfolio of proprietary AI platforms and solutions that are embedded across legal, business and client-facing workflows, helping professionals work more effectively while delivering enhanced value to clients.
Wendell Intelligence – Willkie’s enterprise AI platform, providing a unified interface to AI-powered legal and business workflows
Wendell Financial Insights – a firmwide financial and matter intelligence platform supporting operational and client-service decision-making
Wendell Horizon – an AI-powered professional development and attorney training platform
Wendell Private Funds Secondaries Platform – a specialized solution supporting complex private funds and secondaries workflows
Wendell Class Action Claimant Platform – a technology-enabled platform supporting claimant analysis and litigation workflows

kp.k: Codex integration is intended to accelerate internal legal engineering
kp.d: Willkie expects to integrate OpenAI Codex into its development environment through Willkie Works to accelerate engineers' design, testing and deployment of proprietary tools. OpenAI's Jason Boehmig argues that enabling lawyers and technologists to code will shape legal services; this is his forward-looking view, not evidence of completed integration or demonstrated productivity gains.
qs: The collaboration also extends to OpenAI Codex, which Willkie expects to integrate into its AI development environment through Willkie Works.
These capabilities will help accelerate how the firm's AI engineers design, test and deploy the next generation of proprietary platforms, workflows and client solutions.
The future of legal will be shaped by firms that can put the power of coding directly into the hands of their lawyers and technologists

kp.k: Firm leadership frames AI as service redesign, not speed alone
kp.d: Willkie Chairman Thomas Cerabino argues that AI offers an opportunity to rethink service delivery, use of institutional knowledge and client service. His stated approach combines legal talent with technology rather than articulating lawyer replacement, staffing ratios or a new pricing model.
qs: The opportunity AI presents is not simply to work faster, but to rethink how legal services are delivered, how institutional knowledge is leveraged and how clients are served.
At Willkie, we are achieving this through combining exceptional legal talent with transformative technology to best meet our clients’ needs.

kp.k: Expertise, engineering and governance underpin claimed competitive differentiation
kp.d: Willkie's Chief Digital and Information Officer John Elbasan reports investment in people, governance frameworks and engineering capabilities. He predicts that the greatest AI value will accrue to organisations integrating technology with expertise, workflows and trusted governance, rather than relying on access alone. The press release also reports recent ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification as support for its responsible deployment strategy.
qs: Through Willkie Works, we have invested in the people, governance frameworks and engineering capabilities necessary to transform frontier AI technologies into proprietary platforms that support legal and business workflows across the firm.
The organizations that realize the greatest value from AI will not be defined by access to technology alone.
They will be the ones that can combine frontier AI capabilities with expertise, workflows and trusted governance to create differentiated solutions.

Willkie's AI strategy is supported by a comprehensive governance framework, including its recent achievement of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, reinforcing the firm's commitment to responsible AI innovation and deployment.

kp.k: OpenAI joins a broader, multi-provider AI strategy
kp.d: The press release places OpenAI alongside Willkie's role as a Harvey Innovation Partner and deployment of LexisNexis Protégé. Willkie attributes lasting advantage to integrating, governing and building on multiple innovations through proprietary platforms. Artificial Lawyer compares the arrangement with Freshfields' collaboration with Anthropic and says it does not prevent Willkie from working with other model makers.
qs: The OpenAI collaboration complements Willkie's broader AI strategy, which combines strategic relationships with leading AI innovators and the development of proprietary platforms through Willkie Works.

Alongside collaborations such as the firm's role as a Harvey Innovation Partner and its deployment of LexisNexis Protégé, this approach reflects Willkie's belief that lasting advantage comes from the ability to thoughtfully integrate, govern and build upon the best innovations available to create differentiated solutions for lawyers and clients.
Well, it’s a bit like what Freshfields did with Anthropic, although it doesn’t stop Willkie working with other LLM makers if they want to.

kp.k: Artificial Lawyer speculates about OpenAI's forthcoming legal offering
kp.d: Artificial Lawyer places the collaboration ahead of OpenAI's formal legal-vertical rollout and expects a potential 'Codex for Legal' capability, likened to Claude for Legal. The publication also anticipates incorporation of the legal offering into this relationship and tentatively suggests that Willkie could help OpenAI understand lawyers' needs. These are editorial expectations and speculation, distinct from the announced Codex development integration.
qs: And it’s also expected – by AL – that OpenAI’s legal push will happen via a new ‘Codex for Legal’ *capability – a bit like Claude for Legal.
AL sees this more as a useful step forward for both parties while we all wait for OpenAI to finalise its legal offering, which clearly will then become part of this relationship.
In fact, perhaps this deal will help OpenAI to figure out what lawyers really want…?

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Willkie predicts that its OpenAI collaboration will accelerate proprietary AI development and deployment across legal and business operations.
pts.d: The Willkie press release announces a firmwide ChatGPT Enterprise rollout and says OpenAI frontier models will support the next generation of its proprietary platforms. It also predicts faster platform design, testing and deployment through Codex, whose integration into the Willkie Works development environment is expected rather than reported as completed.

pts.k: Willkie and chairman Thomas Cerabino claim AI can reshape service delivery and the use of institutional knowledge, beyond merely increasing speed.
pts.d: Cerabino describes an ongoing transformation combining legal talent and technology to meet client needs. Separately, the firm claims its existing proprietary platforms already help professionals work more effectively and deliver enhanced client value. These are framed as augmentation of professionals, not as autonomous replacement of lawyers.

pts.k: OpenAI legal vertical product head Jason Boehmig predicts that firms enabling lawyers and technologists to build tools will shape the future of legal services.
pts.d: Boehmig claims frontier models and Codex create a genuinely new ability to turn firm expertise into tools tailored to professionals' work and client service. His prediction concerns software-building capability within firms rather than a demonstrated change in legal-market shares or employment.

pts.k: Willkie chief digital and information officer John Elbasan predicts that expertise, workflow integration and governance—not technology access alone—will determine which organizations gain most from AI.
pts.d: Elbasan connects differentiated proprietary solutions to investments in people, engineering and governance. The press release similarly presents lasting advantage as dependent on integrating, governing and building upon external innovations, with OpenAI complementing relationships with Harvey and LexisNexis rather than constituting the firm's sole AI relationship.

pts.k: Artificial Lawyer expects an OpenAI legal offering to become part of the relationship and speculates that the collaboration may inform its development.
pts.d: The article's author expects OpenAI's legal push to take the form of a 'Codex for Legal' capability and characterizes the partnership as a useful step while that offering is finalized. The suggestion that the deal could help OpenAI understand lawyers' needs is explicitly tentative. These are the publication's expectations, not announced product commitments in Willkie's press release.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The principal evidence offered is the firm's reported implementation experience and investments, alongside statements by Willkie and OpenAI executives.
pts.d: The document identifies existing Wendell platforms covering general workflows, financial and matter intelligence, attorney training, private funds secondaries, and class-action claimant analysis. It reports investment in governance and engineering and achievement of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification. These provide implementation context; the document supplies no quantified productivity results, client-outcome measurements, benchmarks or comparative studies establishing the predicted gains. Artificial Lawyer's product forecast is editorial expectation rather than a documented launch commitment.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The sources distinguish existing platform use from prospective rollout and development; they give no completion dates or quantified horizons.
pts.d: Both texts are dated 22 July 2026. The firm's proprietary portfolio and governance investments are described as already in place, while ChatGPT Enterprise expansion, Codex integration and next-generation platform development are forward-looking. Cerabino describes change as ongoing; Boehmig's prediction about the future of legal has no specified horizon. Elbasan conditions superior value on combining AI with expertise, workflows and trusted governance. Artificial Lawyer's forecast depends on OpenAI finalizing its legal offering.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate affected groups are Willkie's lawyers, AI engineers, business professionals and clients; the broader prediction concerns firms able to build and govern tailored AI tools.
pts.d: Lawyers and business professionals are described as gaining expanded AI access and workflow support; attorneys receive AI-powered training support; engineers are expected to design, test and deploy solutions faster. Operational and client-service decision-makers, private-funds teams and litigation teams are named through platform functions. Clients are promised enhanced service and value without quantified benefits. OpenAI may gain insight into lawyers' requirements, according to Artificial Lawyer. The source does not predict headcount reductions, billing changes or access-to-justice effects.
